question: We are considering AEM Sites, AEM Assets, Marketo Engage and Customer Journey Analytics. Explain dependencies and licensing assumptions rather than assuming additional products have been purchased. Our target is to start on 15 February 2027 and release the first market on 2 August 2027, with the other markets following within eight weeks. We expect twelve months of support after the first release.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Your target is to start on 15 February 2027 and release the first market on 2 August 2027, with the other markets following within eight weeks.
- Your email authors pick DAM images in the Email Designer, and changes made in AEM reach your live emails.

How we would do it
- Check with your admins that your Marketo subscription is on Adobe IMS, which the Email Designer needs, and that Dynamic Media with OpenAPI is on.
- Generate the service credential certificate, and link the Delivery tier repository in Marketo Admin.
- Add your email authors to the Assets product profiles, and test that an author can pick a DAM image in the Email Designer.
- Record the certificate's expiry date in a handover note, with a reminder and the steps to renew it, owned by your admin.

What you get
- Linked Delivery tier repository in Marketo
- Email authors in the Assets product profiles
- Connection test results
- Handover note with certificate renewal steps

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 32 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.

Risk we manage
- An expired certificate breaking the link: we record the expiry date, set a reminder and hand your admin the renewal steps.

What we would need from you
- Admins for Marketo Engage and AEM Assets who can make the link
catalog:
Our approach
- AEM Assets is natively integrated with Marketo Engage: an admin links Delivery tier Assets as a Cloud Service repositories with a service credential certificate, and email authors pick DAM images in the Email Designer, where changes made in AEM reach live emails.
- In the new Email Designer, authors place images from a linked AEM Assets Delivery repository (images only); updates in AEM reach live emails without re-uploading, and deleting an image in AEM breaks the emails that use it.
- In Customer Journey Analytics your data can be viewed and analyzed in sequence across channels: data from your call center, point-of-sale systems and online properties is combined into a single reporting view.
- Campaigns run as Smart Campaigns. A Smart List defines who you want to target, using filters and triggers, and the flow sets the steps the campaign performs, including wait steps and split choices.

Licensing this needs
- Your Customer Journey Analytics package: CJA Prime or higher (graph-based stitching).

What we would do
- We will confirm the Marketo subscription is on Adobe IMS (the Email Designer needs it) and Dynamic Media with OpenAPI is on, generate the service credential certificate, link the Delivery tier repository in Marketo Admin, add email authors to the Assets product profiles, and track the certificate expiry.

What we would need from you
- Delivery tier repository in the same IMS org as Marketo Engage.
- HTTPS on every environment that uses remote assets.

question: Describe how you would move our public websites from Drupal to AEM Sites, including how you would decide which pages to retain, merge or retire and demonstrate that retained content and inbound links survived the move.
kb:
How we would do it
- Inventory every page and file on your current site with its traffic and inbound links, and agree with your content owners which to retain, merge or retire.
- Map each content type to the template and components its pages will use, and write the import scripts that build the pages from that map.
- Test the import on each content type with your authors, then load the retained pages in small content packages through Package Manager and their images and files through Bulk Import.
- Build the redirect map for every retired, merged or moved URL, load it as a pipeline-free rewrite map or as Dispatcher or CDN redirect rules, and test every entry.
- Run the final import after the content freeze and publish it, then check sampled pages against the source, crawl for broken links and test the inventory's inbound links.

What you get
- Page inventory with retain, merge and retire decisions
- Content mapping and import scripts
- Published pages, images and files in AEM Sites
- Tested redirect map
- Content, link and redirect check report

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 280 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.
- This also needs an Azure Blob Storage or Amazon S3 account to stage images and files for Bulk Import.
catalog:
Our approach
- How your existing content moves depends on where it sits today. From an existing AEM instance, Adobe's Content Transfer Tool moves it across. From another CMS, we would export the content, map it to the new templates and load it into AEM, agreeing the mapping and tooling with you in discovery.

What we would do
- Where you are moving from a CMS other than AEM, we will list every page and file on the current site with you, agree which pages to retain, merge or retire, and map each content type to the new site's templates and components. We will script the import that builds each retained page on its template, load the pages as content packages through Package Manager, bring their images and files in with Bulk Import, and publish them. We will set up a redirect for every retired, merged or moved URL through a pipeline-free rewrite map or Dispatcher or CDN rules, and test that old URLs and inbound links reach the agreed pages.

question: Explain how our three language versions would be maintained across five markets. Show how a shared product page could receive a local correction without losing that correction when the central team publishes a later update.
kb:
Our approach
- Each country site takes central updates in its own language by rollout, and the corrections your market teams make locally stay in place.

How we would do it
- Map each country site to its language master with your central and market teams, and agree which components each market may correct locally.
- Integrate your translation service provider with AEM, run the first translation projects, then change one source page, send it again and review the updated translation in its launch.
- Deploy the blueprint configuration through the CI/CD pipeline, create each country site as an MSM Live Copy of its language master, and set the agreed rollout configurations.
- Test one shared page per market with its author: break inheritance on a corrected component, roll out a central update, and check the correction stays while other components update.

What you get
- Country sites as MSM Live Copies of language masters
- Translation provider integration and first translation projects
- Blueprint and rollout configurations
- Local correction rules and test results by market

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 80 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.

Risk we manage
- A local correction that also stops later central changes reaching that component: we keep a register of every broken inheritance and review it with each market after central updates.

Our approach
- AEM Sites as a Cloud Service is built on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, with code deployed through Cloud Manager and pages edited visually in the Universal Editor.

question: How would authors and reviewers approve a page before it goes live? Include the treatment of safety wording, an urgent correction outside office hours and evidence showing who approved the published version.
kb:
How we would do it
- Map your review route by site section with your content owners: who writes, who checks legal or safety wording, who approves, and who covers urgent corrections out of hours.
- Remove the replicate right from your author groups, so Sites console publishes become requests, and customize the request workflow with review, legal or safety sign-off and approval steps.
- Assign each step to a group, since a single user's work item cannot be delegated, and add an urgent route your on-call approvers can complete out of hours.
- Keep the workflows non-transient so their history is saved, create a page version at each publish, keep both for your retention period, and test every route with your reviewers.

What you get
- Customized request workflow with an urgent route
- Publish permissions for author and approver groups
- Approval route map by site section
- Approval record kept for your retention period
- Route test results, signed off by your reviewers

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 80 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.

Risk we manage
- A page going live unreviewed: we remove the authors' right to publish, so every change, urgent corrections included, passes an approver and leaves a record.

question: Describe how nightly ERP specification files would reach product pages without exposing trade pricing or stock data. Explain what happens when a file is late, incomplete or contains a value that conflicts with an approved manual.
kb:
How we would do it
- Agree with your product data owner the fields the public site may show, leaving out prices, stock and customer terms, plus the approved values each file must match.
- Build a Content Fragment Model with only those fields, and show each product's fragment on its product page with the Content Fragment Component.
- Build an App Builder application that a cron job runs each night, dropping unlisted fields and writing each passing file to AEM Author through the Content Fragment Management API.
- Hold a late, incomplete or conflicting file with the published values left live, report each run to your product data owner, who publishes from the console, and test each case.

What you get
- Signed-off field list and file checks
- Content Fragment Model and product page display
- Nightly import in App Builder
- Test results, including a file with prices and stock
- Runbook for publishing, held files and alerts

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 80 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.
- This needs Adobe Developer App Builder access.
- This also needs a nightly ERP or PIM export file in a location the import can read.

question: Propose an approach to organising and loading our shared-drive content into AEM Assets. Address duplicate files, superseded manuals, mandatory product and revision fields, and how our engineers would approve the resulting inventory.

question: Our service teams need the correct manual for a particular model, revision and language. Explain how you would make those documents findable and verify that a withdrawn safety certificate cannot still be selected for a new web page.
kb:
How we would do it
- Agree with your document owners which documents carry an expiry date and who approves replacements, and write the runbook: replacements keep the document's name and folder, as new versions.
- List each withdrawn document's pages on its References tab, agree each page's change with its owner, then set the Expires field and unpublish urgent withdrawals at once.
- Run the first replacements with your editors: upload each as a new version, check its pages on the References tab, publish, then test a revert in the Timeline and republish.
- Hide expired assets in the desktop app and Adobe Asset Link where you use them, and test with an author account that expired documents cannot be found or published.

What you get
- Document rules and editor runbook
- Expiry dates on the agreed documents
- First replacements, published and checked page by page
- Test results for expiry, hiding and revert

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 32 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.

Risk we manage
- A document withdrawn while pages still link to it: we list those pages on its References tab first, and each owner agrees the page's change before the expiry date.
catalog:

question: Describe the migration of our active email programmes, subscription choices and suppression records into Marketo Engage. How would you settle conflicting preferences and prove that the first migrated campaign excludes people who should not receive it?
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Your existing email platform contains subscription preferences and suppression lists that do not always agree with Salesforce.

How we would do it
- Inventory your active email programs, subscription types and suppression records, and agree with your legal team which choice wins when sources or the CRM conflict, such as the most restrictive.
- Create a custom field for each subscription type and the subscription center, then import your people and their choices, checking a sample file against the export first.
- Set Unsubscribed, Marketing Suspended or Blocklisted with Change Data Value flow steps on every record holding a suppressed address, and mark old hard bounces as Email Invalid.
- Rebuild your active programs with no marketing email set as operational, and before the first migrated send, check its blocked people and that its recipients include no suppressed address.

What you get
- Program, preference and suppression inventory
- Conflict rule and decision log
- People, choices and suppression flags in Marketo Engage
- Subscription center and rebuilt active programs
- Pre-send check record for the first migrated campaign

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 96 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.
- This also needs exports of people, subscription choices and suppression records from the current email platform.

question: Explain how a website enquiry would pass through Marketo Engage and Salesforce to the correct dealer-facing sales team. Cover existing contacts, repeated submissions, territory changes and a failed transfer that otherwise leaves an enquiry unanswered.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: You have 65 web authors, 18 reviewers, 12 marketing operators and 160 dealer-facing sales staff.
- Marketo Engage and your CRM share the right data, with an agreed mapping, hidden fields kept hidden and a tested sync.

How we would do it
- Agree the field mapping with your CRM admin before the first sync, field by field, in a mapping sheet that records owners and data types.
- Connect Marketo Engage to Salesforce with your CRM admin, and choose which fields sync and which stay hidden.
- Check that the sync is running correctly after the first sync, comparing a sample of records in both systems against the mapping sheet.
- Record the final mapping, hidden fields and sync settings in a sync runbook, with who to call and what to check when records stop syncing.

What you get
- Agreed field mapping sheet
- Marketo Engage connected to your CRM
- Sync test results and sync runbook

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 60 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.

Risk we manage
- A wrong mapping at the first sync puts bad values in many records at once: we agree every field with your CRM admin before it runs.

What we would need from you
- A CRM admin who can agree the mapping and set up the connection
catalog:
Our approach
- We would configure the admin settings, including CNAMEs and Marketo's JavaScript tracking code, Munchkin, which tracks the people who visit your website so that automated campaigns can react to their visits. We would test the automation workflows and the data sync before launch.
- Where your CRM is Salesforce, the sync is bidirectional for leads, contacts and Salesforce campaigns, so a change made in either system is reflected in both. All other syncs run from Salesforce to Marketo only.

What we would do
- We will run a data audit, build the program that standardizes incoming data, and model lead scoring and the lead lifecycle with marketing and sales, through to the MQL handoff.

question: Describe how you would define and collect the website and enquiry events needed for Customer Journey Analytics. Explain how you would check that a download, a completed enquiry and an abandoned form are counted consistently across markets without collecting free-text form contents.
kb:
How we would do it
- Agree the page data to collect with your analytics team, starting with page name, site section and host, and record it in a measurement plan.
- Add a Tags rule on the Adobe Client Data Layer's cmp:show event that sends each page view with Web SDK to Platform Edge Network.
- Check that page views reach the Experience Platform dataset with every agreed field, then add the dataset to your CJA connection and data view.
- Agree with your analytics team which buttons and teaser CTAs to track, and how each CTA's ID and name should read in reports.
- Add a Tags rule on the data layer's click event for those buttons and teaser CTAs, sending the CTA ID and name with Web SDK.
- Click through a test set of CTAs, check each click arrives in the Experience Platform dataset, then add the CTA fields to your CJA data view.

What you get
- Tags property connected to AEM
- Data elements and page view rule
- Page views in the dataset and CJA data view
- Tags rule for button and teaser CTA clicks
- CTA clicks in the dataset and CJA data view

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 48 hours.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.

question: We want to understand the path from an anonymous website visit to an enquiry and a later sales outcome recorded in Salesforce. question: Set out how you would assess and correct accessibility issues in the new page templates, enquiry forms and published documents. Our acceptance target is WCAG 2.2 AA; distinguish automated checks from manual checks and identify who would verify completion.
kb:
Our approach
- You told us: Your acceptance target is WCAG 2.2 AA.

How we would do it
- Agree WCAG 2.2 Level AA as the target with your team, then audit your current templates and a sample of pages and record each gap.
- Build each component and template to meet every Level A and AA success criterion, including visible focus, target size, color contrast, headings, form labels and text alternatives.
- Test every template with an automated scan, keyboard-only use and screen readers such as NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver, and log each issue against its WCAG success criterion.
- Train your authors to write alternative text, headings, link text and table headers, with a checklist to run before they publish each page.
- Set a release gate: each release passes an automated scan and a manual keyboard and screen reader check of changed templates, with no new A or AA failures.

What you get
- Accessibility audit of templates and sample pages
- WCAG 2.2 AA test plan and release checklist
- Issue log mapped to WCAG success criteria
- Author guide and checklist for accessible content

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: about 60 to 240 hours for this work.
- This runs during the build, once discovery has agreed the scope, ahead of your launch on 2 August 2027.

question: Describe the monthly service you would provide after launch for the four proposed Adobe products and their integrations. Include incident ownership, monitoring, routine changes, release checks, monthly reporting and a clear boundary between the recurring fee and separately estimated work.
kb:
Our approach
- Your site keeps receiving code releases through Cloud Manager each month, with issues found in the logs and fixed.

How we would do it
- Ship the month's code changes through the Cloud Manager pipelines, once reviewed and tested with your team.
- Check each automatic AEM version update, and review the logs every week, within the seven days Cloud Manager keeps them, with the Developer Console for errors.
- Fix the issues we find, and report the month's releases, issues and fixes to your team.
- Add, change and remove user access as your teams change, and log each change for your administrators.
- Review Admin, Marketing Activities, Design Studio and Database each month against a standing checklist for clean-up, deliverability and scoring changes.
- Run flow, fallout and attribution analysis on those journeys in Analysis Workspace, breaking results down by dimension where that explains a change.

What you get
- Monthly code releases through Cloud Manager
- Weekly log review and update check
- Monthly asset report summary
- Monthly instance review report
- Monthly journey analysis in Analysis Workspace

Timeline and effort
- Planning estimate: 88 hours a month.
- This runs every month from the month after your launch on 2 August 2027.

Risk we manage
- Problems going unnoticed after go-live: we review the logs every week, within the seven days Cloud Manager keeps them, and check every automatic AEM version update.
catalog:
Our approach
- After launch we provide these services each month, product by product.

After launch
- Customer Journey Analytics: each month we will run flow, fallout and attribution analysis on priority journeys, report findings to stakeholders and recommend next actions.
- Marketo Engage: each month we will review Admin, Marketing Activities, Design Studio and Database for clean-up, deliverability and scoring changes, and agree the fixes with your Marketo owner.
- AEM Assets: each month we will review asset reports on usage and sharing, tidy metadata and tags, update processing profiles and manage user access.
- AEM Sites: each month we will ship code through Cloud Manager pipelines, check the automatic AEM version updates, review logs and the Developer Console, and fix issues found after go-live.

question: Provide a proposed hosting and data-flow diagram showing production and non-production environments, countries in which our data would be stored or processed, and the responsibilities of your firm, Adobe and our existing providers. Identify any location or service detail still requiring confirmation.
catalog:
Where your data is hosted
- Customer Journey Analytics: on Adobe Experience Platform, on Microsoft Azure or Amazon Web Services.¹,²,³ You choose the region (North America, Europe or Asia Pacific) at provisioning; data cannot be moved later.⁴
- Marketo Engage: on AWS, in a single region.⁵,⁶
- AEM Assets and AEM Sites: you choose the primary region at setup, for example the US, Canada, the UK, Germany or Australia; it cannot be changed afterwards.⁷,⁸

What we would need from you
- The region your data must stay in, since the region is chosen at setup and cannot be moved later.

question: Explain how you would control staff and supplier access to the proposed environments, including single sign-on, privileged access, service credentials, joiners and leavers, and an auditable review of permissions. Our security team must approve production access before it is granted.
catalog:
Security certifications and encryption
- Customer Journey Analytics, Marketo Engage, AEM Assets and AEM Sites: Adobe's Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 22301 and CSA STAR Level 2 for Adobe Experience Cloud, which includes these products.¹,² The list also marks Adobe Experience Cloud GLBA ready; you remain responsible for your own compliance.¹
- Customer Journey Analytics: all data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2) and at rest.³,⁴
- Marketo Engage: every instance is encrypted at rest with AES 256-bit.⁵
- AEM Assets and AEM Sites: provider-managed encryption keys by default; customer-managed keys are available.⁶

Sign-in and single sign-on
- Your team signs in to the Adobe products in this proposal through the Adobe Admin Console. Single sign-on uses Federated IDs with any SAML 2.0 identity provider, such as Okta, Ping Identity or AD FS, or with Microsoft Entra ID over OpenID Connect.⁷,⁸
- Customer Journey Analytics: access is controlled with roles and policies that link users with permissions and sandboxes.⁹

What we would need from you
- The identity provider your team signs in with, such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID.
